title: Graphics
summary: What the graphics settings in Options do, and which to turn off on a slow device.
text:
The **Graphics** part of **Options** (☰ menu, or ⚙ on the title screen) changes only how the game looks, never how it plays.

- **Sky reflections**: metal and glass mirror the sky and catch glints of the sun, and the sky lights everything softly from all round. Cheap on any device
- **Ambient occlusion**: soft shade where things meet: under vehicles, round buildings, in creases and among plants. On by default on computers, off on phones
- **Sun shadows**: up close, the sun casts real shadows: vehicles, buildings, plants and hills shade each other and themselves (zoomed out, the soft **Ground shadows** take over). On by default on computers, off on phones
- **Glow**: lights, glow strips and gunfire spill soft light
- **Mist and sun haze**: on worlds with air, mist gathers in low ground in the distance, thickest round sunrise and sunset, and the haze glows warm toward a low sun
- **Terrain look**: **Smooth** (the default) shades the land softly, with ground textures and bare rock on steep slopes; **Flat** shows crisp low-poly facets

With **Ambient occlusion** on, **Anti-aliasing** on Auto or MSAA smooths edges with SMAA instead (the two can't work together).

If a phone runs hot or slow, turn off **Glow**, **Ambient occlusion**, **Sun shadows** and **Weather** first. **Performance stats** (under Interface) shows the frame rate while you try.
